SEPARATION AGREEMENT AND GENERAL RELEASE

This Separation Agreement and General Release (this "Agreement") is entered into effective as of November 14, 2025 (the "Effective Date"), by and between MERIDIAN MECHANICAL OF ILLINOIS, LLC, an Illinois limited liability company located at 1455 Busse Road, Elk Grove Village, Illinois 60007 ("Company"), and HECTOR BANCROFT, an individual ("Employee").

RECITALS

WHEREAS, Employee has been employed by Company as a Lead Installation Technician at Company's Naperville branch since on or about June 7, 2021; and

WHEREAS, Company has determined that Employee's position is being eliminated due to operational restructuring and business necessity, and it is not feasible to retain Employee in an alternative position within Company; and

WHEREAS, Company and Employee desire to effect a separation of employment relationship on the terms and conditions set forth herein, including Employee's receipt of severance benefits and Employee's execution of this Agreement and General Release.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, Company and Employee agree as follows:

1. SEPARATION DATE

1.1 Employee's last day of active employment with Company shall be December 19, 2025 (the "Separation Date"). Effective as of the Separation Date, Employee shall cease to be an employee of Company and shall have no further right to compensation, benefits, or other emoluments from Company except as expressly provided in this Agreement. Employee's employment with Company is hereby terminated without cause due to position elimination.

1.2 Employee shall cooperate fully with Company during the period from the Effective Date through the Separation Date to facilitate a smooth transition of Employee's duties and responsibilities. Such cooperation shall include, but is not limited to, training designated replacement personnel, transferring all work-related information and files, and completing all outstanding work assignments to the extent reasonably practicable.

1.3 As of the Separation Date, all keys, identification badges, tools owned by Company, mobile devices, laptops, tablets, and all other property of Company in Employee's possession or control shall be returned to Company in good working condition, normal wear and tear excepted. Employee shall cooperate with Company's information technology department to ensure that all Company systems access is promptly disabled and all Company data is removed from Employee's personal devices.

2. SEVERANCE

2.1 In consideration for Employee's execution and non-revocation of this Agreement and General Release (as defined below), Company shall provide to Employee severance pay equal to six weeks of Employee's regular hourly compensation, calculated at Employee's average hourly rate as of the Effective Date, for a total severance payment of ten thousand one hundred fifty dollars ($10,150.00) (the "Severance Amount").

2.2 The Severance Amount shall be paid in a lump sum via Employee's established payroll method within five business days following the expiration of the Review Period (as defined in Section 6 below) and Employee's execution of this Agreement without revocation, provided Employee is in compliance with all terms and conditions hereof.

2.3 The Severance Amount is conditioned upon and contingent upon Employee signing this Agreement and not revoking this Agreement during the Review Period. If Employee revokes this Agreement pursuant to Section 6.3 hereof, Employee shall receive no Severance Amount and shall forfeit all rights hereunder except as expressly provided by law.

2.4 All payments made pursuant to this Section 2 shall be subject to applicable tax withholding and payroll deductions required by federal, state, and local law. Company shall issue an IRS Form W-2 for the year of separation reflecting the Severance Amount.

2.5 Employee shall not be entitled to receive any other severance, separation pay, bonus, or other compensation beyond what is expressly set forth in this Agreement. Employee acknowledges that the Severance Amount represents full and complete satisfaction of any severance obligations of Company to Employee.

2.6 Employee shall forfeit any accrued paid time off, personal days, or unused vacation days as of the Separation Date, which shall not be paid out or carried forward. Employee waives any claim to payment for such accrued but unused time off.

3. GENERAL RELEASE

3.1 In exchange for the Severance Amount and the other consideration provided in this Agreement, and except as expressly preserved in Section 3.2 below, Employee, on behalf of himself and his heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and assigns, hereby irrevocably and unconditionally releases, waives, and forever discharges Company and its parent, subsidiary, and affiliated entities, and each of their respective past and present owners, members, officers, directors, managers, employees, agents, attorneys, and representatives from any and all claims, demands, liabilities, causes of action, whether known or unknown, arising out of or in any way related to Employee's employment relationship with Company or the termination thereof, including but not limited to any claims for unpaid wages, overtime compensation, bonuses, benefits, breach of contract, wrongful termination, discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or any other legal theory under federal, state, or local law.

3.2 Notwithstanding the release in Section 3.1, Employee does not release and expressly preserves the following: (a) any rights to benefits earned or vested under any qualified pension or retirement plan sponsored by Company, including the right to receive such benefits in accordance with the terms of such plans; (b) any rights under this Agreement; (c) any rights that are not legally waivable; (d) any rights to indemnification under Company's Bylaws, Operating Agreement, or Delaware, Illinois or applicable state law for acts performed in an official capacity; and (e) any claims arising after the date of Employee's execution of this Agreement.

3.3 This General Release includes, without limitation, a complete release of any and all claims that Employee may have under the Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967, as amended, 29 U.S.C. Section 621 et seq. ("ADEA"). Employee hereby acknowledges that he has been advised, as required by the Older Workers Benefit Protection Act ("OWBPA"), that he may have rights under the ADEA and that this Agreement may affect such rights. Employee has been given an opportunity to consult with an attorney regarding this Agreement and the release of ADEA rights. Employee further acknowledges that the Severance Amount provided under Section 2 exceeds what Employee would be entitled to receive under any applicable Company severance policy or practice.

3.4 Employee hereby releases any and all claims arising under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Americans with Disabilities Act, Section 501 of the Rehabilitation Act, the Civil Rights Act of 1991, the Equal Pay Act, the Fair Labor Standards Act, the Illinois Human Rights Act, the Illinois Minimum Wage Law, the Illinois Wage Payment Act, the Illinois Whistleblower Protection Act, and any other federal, state, or local statute, regulation, or common law doctrine, except to the extent such release is prohibited by applicable law.

4. CONTINUING OBLIGATIONS

4.1 Non-Competition. Employee acknowledges and reaffirms his obligations under the Non-Competition covenant contained in the Technician Employment Agreement dated June 7, 2021 (the "Original Employment Agreement"), which covenant remains in full force and effect. Employee shall continue to comply with the non-competition restrictions set forth in the Original Employment Agreement following the Separation Date. Specifically, and without limitation of the foregoing, Employee agrees that for a period of twelve months following the Separation Date, Employee shall not, without the prior written consent of Company, either directly or indirectly, engage in any business, capacity, or position with any person or entity that is engaged in the business of providing plumbing, heating, ventilation, air conditioning, mechanical contracting services, or similar services within a fifty-mile radius of Company's Naperville branch location, including but not limited to any business of substantially similar nature or type to that of Company.

4.2 Non-Solicitation. Employee acknowledges and reaffirms his obligations under the Non-Solicitation covenant contained in the Original Employment Agreement, which covenant remains in full force and effect. Employee shall continue to comply with the non-solicitation restrictions set forth in the Original Employment Agreement following the Separation Date. Specifically, and without limitation of the foregoing, Employee agrees that for a period of twelve months following the Separation Date, Employee shall not, without the prior written consent of Company, directly or indirectly solicit, contact, recruit, encourage, or attempt to recruit or encourage any employee or independent contractor of Company to leave Company's employ or to accept employment or enter into an independent contractor relationship with any competitor or alternative business.

4.3 Confidential Information. Employee reaffirms and continues to be bound by all confidentiality obligations imposed by the Original Employment Agreement and applicable law. Employee acknowledges that he possesses knowledge of confidential and proprietary information of Company, including but not limited to customer lists, pricing information, business methods, trade secrets, technical data, operational procedures, financial information, and other confidential business information not generally known to the public. Employee shall maintain the confidentiality of all such information and shall not, at any time following the Separation Date, disclose, use, or permit the disclosure or use of any such confidential information, except as authorized by Company or as required by law.

4.4 Return of Confidential Materials. Employee represents and warrants that he has returned or will return to Company prior to the Separation Date all documents, files, customer information, business records, and other materials containing confidential or proprietary information of Company. Employee shall not retain any copies of such materials in any form, whether physical, electronic, or otherwise.

4.5 These continuing obligations are in addition to, and do not limit, any other non-competition, non-solicitation, or confidentiality obligations imposed upon Employee by the Original Employment Agreement or applicable law, all of which remain in full force and effect.

5. REVIEW PERIOD

5.1 Employee shall have twenty-one (21) calendar days from the Effective Date (expiring on December 5, 2025) to review this Agreement and consider whether to execute it (the "Review Period"). Company encourages Employee to consult with an attorney of Employee's choice regarding this Agreement and its consequences prior to execution.

5.2 Employee is advised that he has the right to consult with legal counsel prior to signing this Agreement and that the costs of such consultation shall be borne by Employee. The Review Period is intended to satisfy the requirements of the OWBPA and the ADEA.

5.3 If Employee decides to execute this Agreement, Employee shall sign and date this Agreement on the signature page provided below at any time during or after the Review Period. Once executed, Employee shall have an additional seven (7) calendar days from the date of his signature within which to revoke this Agreement by providing written notice of revocation to Company's Human Resources Department at 1455 Busse Road, Elk Grove Village, Illinois 60007 (the "Revocation Period"). The notice must be hand-delivered or postmarked by the end of the seventh day following Employee's execution of this Agreement.

5.4 In order for revocation to be effective, Company must receive actual written notice of revocation within the Revocation Period. If Employee does not timely revoke this Agreement, Employee shall be conclusively presumed to have accepted this Agreement in its entirety, and the agreement shall become fully binding and enforceable.

5.5 The 21-day Review Period and 7-day Revocation Period are in addition to any review period required by applicable law and are intended to ensure that Employee has adequate time and opportunity to understand the consequences of this Agreement.

6. GOVERNING LAW

6.1 This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Illinois, without regard to conflicts of law principles. Employee and Company hereby consent to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Cook County, Illinois and the United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois for resolution of any disputes arising out of this Agreement.

6.2 The parties acknowledge that the covenants contained in Section 4 above, including the non-competition and non-solicitation obligations, are governed by the terms of the Original Employment Agreement dated June 7, 2021, and any reference to such covenants in this Agreement shall be construed consistently with the terms thereof and applicable Illinois law.

7. ENTIRE AGREEMENT

This Agreement, together with the Original Employment Agreement insofar as it relates to continuing obligations, constitutes the entire agreement between Company and Employee regarding the subject matter hereof and supersedes any and all prior understandings and agreements, whether written or oral. No modification, amendment, or supplement to this Agreement shall be valid or binding unless made in writing and executed by both Company and Employee. If any provision of this Agreement is found to be invalid or unenforceable, such provision shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable, and the remainder of this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect.

8. MISCELLANEOUS

8.1 This Agreement may not be assigned by either party without the prior written consent of the other party. The rights and obligations hereunder shall inure to the benefit of and be binding upon the parties and their respective successors and assigns.

8.2 No waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the waiving party. No waiver of any breach or default of this Agreement shall constitute a waiver of any other breach or default.

8.3 Employee acknowledges that he has read this Agreement in its entirety, understands its terms and conditions, has had the opportunity to consult with legal counsel, and is voluntarily entering into this Agreement with full knowledge of its consequences and with the intent to be legally bound thereby.

8.4 Employee shall not make any disparaging or negative statements about Company, its business, reputation, management, or operations to any third party, including but not limited to prospective employers, customers, vendors, or social media, except to the extent such statements are truthful and necessary to defend Employee's interests in any legal proceeding.

8.5 The section headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation or construction of this Agreement.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.
